transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from "NPR News in Washington," I'm Windsor Johnston.
♪♪
The nation is pausing to honor American service members
on this Veterans Day.
At Arlington National Cemetery, President Trump spoke about
the sacrifices behind the country's freedoms.
>> Americans must always remember that our way of life
is not the natural condition of mankind.
Everything we've achieved, everything that we are,
everything that we hope to become is built on the courage
of those willing to endure and unimaginable and to some just unbearable
and to stand strong when all else gives way.
>> Earlier, service members took part in the ceremony.
>> Re-vets! >> Re-vets!
>> Off!
>> The president and First Lady also laid a wreath at the tomb
of the unknown soldier as veterans and military families were in attendance.
Beyond the nation's capital, Americans are honoring vets with ceremonies
and commemorations across the country.
NPR's Quill Lawrence is at a parade in New York City.
He reports the holiday is offering a look at how military service
has changed across generations.
>> It's day to mark the people who served this country in the military.
At the same time, the number of veterans in this country are shrinking,
even in the Congress that just got elected.
We have more women veterans than ever, but the number of vets in Congress
keep shrinking as the massive numbers of people who served in wars
like World War II, Korea, Vietnam, those who were drafted,
those numbers shrink to the pretty tiny number of veterans who served
in the all-volunteer force.
And the incoming Congress will have only about 15% veterans
down from 30, 40 years ago when Congress was upwards of 70% veterans.
>> NPR's Quill Lawrence.
Peace talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have ended without a breakthrough.
NPR's Hunter Beardsley reports President Trump's envoys are now traveling to Russia.
>> Had U.S. negotiator and President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner
told the media they had seen some openings and opportunities,
but few in Ukraine believe a window for serious diplomacy has opened.
Skeptical Ukrainian negotiators were instructed to approach the talks
with an open mind if only to avoid annoying President Trump.
Ukrainians do not believe the Kremlin will miss the opportunity
to pummel Ukraine's severely weakened energy infrastructure
in this fifth winter of the war.
Analysts say Trump is looking for a foreign policy win after his midterm drubbing,
but Putin has not backed off any of his maximalist demands,
such as Kiev handing over territory Russia has been unable to conquer.
Eleanor Beardsley in PR News, Kiev.
>> This is NPR News.
State officials in Pennsylvania have reported more than 1,500 measles cases
so far this year.
There are six confirmed measles-related deaths.
The greatest number of cases are in Lancaster County,
home to many in the Amish community.
NPR's Maria Godoy reports health officials are reaching out
with a quiet vaccination campaign.
>> Surveys suggest only about a third of Amish families
in Lancaster County vaccinate their children,
often for cultural and practical rather than religious reasons.
But as measles spreads, health officials have been building trust
by vaccinating Amish people in their homes
and hosting frequent vaccine clinics advertised solely by word of mouth.
Dr. Jennifer Wallace is with the Pennsylvania Department of Health.
>> They tend to be a community that does not want to have a lot of big hoopla,
but also the choice to vaccinate they consider to be a very private one.
>> She says the state will keep on offering these low-key vaccinations
for as long as people want them.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
>> Hundreds of schools in Italy were evacuated today following
emailed bomb threats.
Threatening messages also reached schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland
and the Republic of Ireland.
Authorities are investigating who sent the emails.
Italy's Education Minister says the threats do not appear
to represent a genuine danger.
Police elsewhere also described the messages as likely hoaxes
with schools generally remaining open.
On Wall Street, the Dow was up 68 points.
This is NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: President Trump speaks at Arlington National Cemetery on Veterans Day, honoring service members' sacrifices
Quill Lawrence reports on Veterans Day parade in New York City and shrinking veteran representation in Congress
Peace talks on ending the war in Ukraine end without breakthrough; US envoys traveling to Russia
Pennsylvania reports over 1,500 measles cases this year, with six deaths, concentrated in Lancaster County's Amish community
Hundreds of schools in Italy evacuated after emailed bomb threats; similar threats reach Scotland and Ireland
